seoDescription: Learn to build a complete Angular login and signup page from scratch. This comprehensive tutorial guides you through creating the UI with an HTML template, managing state with template-driven forms, and binding data using ngModel. You'll implement signup functionality by saving user data to local storage, handling data persistence with JSON.stringify and JSON.parse. The video also covers implementing the login logic, validating credentials against stored data, and debugging common issues for a functional application.

chapters.description: This chapter introduces the goal of building an Angular login and signup page using a pre-built template and local storage for data persistence.

chapters.title: Creating Data Models for Signup & Login
chapters.description: This chapter covers creating the necessary arrays and objects in the component's TypeScript file to hold signup and login form data.

chapters.title: Binding Form Inputs with ngModel
chapters.description: This chapter demonstrates how to bind the HTML form inputs to the component's data models using the ngModel directive.

chapters.title: Implementing the Signup Functionality
chapters.description: This chapter covers writing the `onSignUp` method to push new user data into an array and save it to local storage.

chapters.title: Fixing the Signup Data Replication Bug
chapters.description: This chapter identifies and fixes a bug where stale data was being replicated by re-initializing the signup object after each submission.

chapters.title: Reading Data from Local Storage on Init
chapters.description: This chapter explains how to use the ngOnInit lifecycle hook to load existing user data from local storage when the component initializes.

chapters.title: Implementing the Login Logic
chapters.description: This chapter details how to implement the `onLogin` method, using the array find method to check for a user with matching credentials.

chapters.title: Testing and Debugging the Login Flow
chapters.description: This chapter walks through debugging the login process, testing both successful and failed login attempts to verify the logic.

chapters.title: Conclusion and Final Thoughts
chapters.description: This final chapter summarizes the local storage implementation and discusses how this logic can be adapted to use a real API.

summary:
## Project Overview
This video tutorial demonstrates how to build a functional **Login and Signup** page in **Angular**. It uses a pre-built HTML/CSS template and leverages browser **local storage** for data persistence, simulating a backend for a client-side only application.

## Data Models & State Management
Two primary objects are created to manage the state of the forms:
- **`signUpObject`**: Bound to the signup form, containing `username`, `email`, and `password`.
- **`loginObject`**: Bound to the login form, containing `username` and `password`.
- **`signUpUsers[]`**: An array to store all registered user objects.

> [!TIP]
> While the tutorial uses `any` for simplicity, it's best practice to create strongly-typed `class` or `interface` definitions for your data models.

## Form Binding
- **Template-driven forms** are used to connect the HTML inputs to the component's data models.
- The **`ngModel`** directive is used for two-way data binding.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> To use `ngModel`, you must import `FormsModule` into your `app.module.ts` and add it to the `imports` array.

## Sign Up Logic
1.  The `onSignUp()` method is triggered on form submission.
2.  The current `signUpObject` is pushed into the `signUpUsers` array.
3.  The entire `signUpUsers` array is stored in local storage.
4.  **`localStorage.setItem('key', value)`** is used to store the data.
5.  The array is converted to a string using **`JSON.stringify()`** before being stored, as local storage only accepts string values.

## Login Logic
1.  The `onLogin()` method is triggered on login submission.
2.  It uses the JavaScript **`array.find()`** method on the `signUpUsers` array.
3.  It searches for an object where both the `username` and `password` match the values from the `loginObject`.
4.  If a user is found, a success message is shown. Otherwise, a "wrong credentials" error is displayed.

## Important Concepts & Fixes

### Data Persistence with `ngOnInit`
- On component initialization (**`ngOnInit`**), the application checks local storage for existing user data.
- If data is found with **`localStorage.getItem('key')`**, it's parsed back into a JavaScript object using **`JSON.parse()`** and used to populate the `signUpUsers` array. This ensures user data persists across page reloads.

### Fixing a Data Reference Bug
- **Problem**: When signing up multiple users, all entries in the `signUpUsers` array were identical to the last user added.
- **Cause**: The `signUpObject` was being pushed by reference. Without being re-initialized, subsequent changes to the form fields also modified the object already in the array.
- **Solution**: After pushing the object to the array, **re-initialize the `signUpObject`** to a new, empty object. This breaks the reference and ensures each signup is a unique entry.
  ```typescript
  // Inside onSignUp()
  this.signUpUsers.push(this.signUpObject);
  // ... store in localStorage ...
  this.signUpObject = { username: '', email: '', password: '' }; // Crucial fix!
  ```
